VAMP contains two binding motifs for botulinum neurooxins D and F, which differ in the residues involved in the interaction with the two toxins.
botulinum D and F neurotoxins recognize the two VAMP domains V1 and V1 in different ways.
V1 is a major determinant of the interaction between VAMP and botulinum neurootoxins D and E and that V2 also plays a role in the recognition of the two endopeptides.

the interaction of botulinum neurootoxins D and E with their specific receptor, the vesicle associated membrane protein (VAMP) which is a component of synaptic vesicles.
the interaction between the botulinum neuro‐toxins and their receptors, the synaptic vesicle proteins VAMP and syntaxin.
the interaction of botulinum neurooxins D and F with VAMP/synatobrevin and provides new insights into the molecular mechanism of neuroexocytosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

VAMP contains two independent and distinct binding sites for tetanus toxin and for botulinum toxins B and G, and two partially overlapping and partially distinct sites for botulinum neurootoxins D and E, while the binding site for botulinum toxin F appears to be a composite of both the V1 and the V2 motifs.
the V1/V2 motif of VAMP is a recognition site for the botulinum neuro‐toxins D, F and G.
botulinum neurootoxins B, G, and D recognize VAMP through the V1 and/or V2 motif, while tetanus toxin binds VAMP through the second motif.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
V1 is the primary determinant of VAMP recognition, V2 is a secondary determinant and that the pairing of V1 and 2 segments is important for the interaction of VAMP with botulinum D and F neurotoxins.
the V1 and the V2 segments, together with the C‐terminal region, are involved in VAMP recognition.
the two neurotoxins recognize different VAMP epitopes, which are located at the two ends of the protein.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the V1 and the V2 segments are not equivalent and that they are involved in different aspects of the VAMP–neurotoxin interaction.
the VAMP‐toxin interaction is more complex than previously thought.
